cand.organizationName: University of Toronto / Canadian Association of Radiologists event listing

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Two relevant relationship candidates: Dr. Tanya Chawla, publicly identified as AIEC director and Virtual Colonography faculty; and Caitlin Gillan, identified on the institutional AIEC page as its manager. Chawla can connect the hotel to course leadership; Gillan is the stronger operational-routing candidate. Neither is verified as a hotel contracting signatory, accommodation buyer or January 2027 budget holder. Start through the course-published aiec@uhn.ca and ask for the current programme/accommodation administrator.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming in-person course, January 11–13, 2027, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. CAR publishes January 11 at 8:00 a.m. through January 13 at 5:00 p.m. EST; these are activity dates, not publication dates. The University course page independently confirms the date range. “Virtual” describes colonography, not remote participation. No later edition through June 2028 was identified in the official sources reviewed.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: low fit for the original local_catering_day_meetings segment, but possible very small attendee/faculty lodging fit. AIEC publishes maximum class size of 12 students; this is centre capacity, not January enrolment or total attendance. The course already uses individual imaging workstations and hospital facilities and includes daily continental breakfast. Its likely lodging scale is materially below the hotel’s approximately 15–109 peak-room target; no room count can be forecast without attendee origin and faculty requirements. A 157-room hotel could accommodate a small subset without a capacity problem, but a ballroom or exclusive housing proposal is disproportionate. Urban hospital access matters more than resort positioning. Do not promise catering or restaurant availability; those hotel capabilities remain unverified.
findings.venueCommitments: Published venue: Advanced Imaging and Education Centre, Toronto General Hospital, Peter Munk Building, Room 1 PMB 166, 585 University Avenue, Toronto, Ontario M5G 2N2, Canada. This is Toronto proper, downtown hospital district—not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. CAR identifies AIEC/Toronto General Hospital for the January edition; the University supplies the room-level AIEC address. This is a published venue assignment, not evidence of an executed venue contract. The 263 McCaul Street departmental footer is not the event venue.
findings.historicalRotation: Recent published timeline: June 5–7 and November 20–22, 2023; May 13–15 and November 25–27, 2024; October 27–29, 2025; February 9–11, March 31–April 2 and October 26–28, 2026; next January 11–13, 2027. CAR explicitly locates the March/April and October 2026 editions at Toronto General Hospital/AIEC. Earlier dates are listed by the University without separate edition-specific venue confirmation. This establishes repeated courses, not a fixed annual cadence or destination-rotation programme. No recent alternate host hotel or destination rotation was established.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Published pathway is attendee-direct hotel reservations with a possible University rate, not a demonstrated housing bureau or contracted block. Exact University wording: “Many hotels will honour a discounted U of T rate, if available, so please mention when booking.” The only hotel named in its accommodation section is Doubletree by Hilton Hotel, 108 Chestnut Street; it says “remember to ask for the U of T rate” and gives direct reservation details. Toronto Tourism is an information referral, not evidence of a housing-bureau appointment. These are general course-page recommendations, not January 2027 inventory commitments. No edition-specific room allocation, cutoff, room-night commitment, open RFP or exclusive hotel agreement was found. January registration details could not be independently inspected.
findings.organizationStructure: University-led medical continuing education: the University of Toronto Department of Medical Imaging publishes the course, and AIEC operates within Toronto General Hospital/JDMI. CAR lists it as an “Other” organizer event and states it is offered by the University of Toronto; CAR should not be treated as the event owner or hotel buyer. No appointed PCO, DMC, agency or housing contractor was identified. Vitrea is the published training platform, not a hotel-sourcing intermediary.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The course page recommends Doubletree by Hilton Hotel at 108 Chestnut Street for proximity to Toronto General Hospital. That is an incumbent referral advantage, not a verified exclusive booking commitment. The hospital-based teaching facilities and included breakfast constrain a hotel day-meeting/catering pitch. No sold-out dates, overflow need, room compression or unmet inventory were published. Do not characterize this as convention overflow.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Low-priority qualification outreach to aiec@uhn.ca, addressed to Caitlin Gillan/current AIEC programme manager, with Dr. Tanya Chawla as the leadership relationship route. Ask whether January 11–13 participants or faculty need overnight accommodation, how many are nonlocal, who handles hotel referrals, whether the Doubletree recommendation entails any agreement, and whether an optional Radisson rate/link may be circulated. Quote only after demand is known. If January has no need, request permission to discuss future published AIEC course dates; do not send an unsolicited venue-replacement or catering proposal.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: January 2027 teaching venue is already assigned to the hospital. Accommodation remains commercially unconfirmed: public information supports direct booking guidance, not an open procurement exercise. A modest nonexclusive lodging/referral conversation may be possible, but permission to market to attendees, remaining accommodation needs and any existing rate agreements must be confirmed.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: repeated small courses support a programme-level accommodation referral/rate relationship more plausibly than capturing the teaching venue. Offer an optional Harbourfront lodging alternative for nonlocal participants or visiting faculty only if the administrator confirms demand and acceptable travel to the hospital. No later dates or movable venue opportunity are established; do not create a 2028 edition or annual room forecast.
